definitions.definition: biopsy technique using extreme cold to obtain larger tissue samples

technology_and_technique.description: Bronchoscopes ≤3.5 mm diameter, reaching 5th-generation bronchi and beyond. New-generation models have 1.7 mm channels allowing rEBUS probes.
Ultrathin bronchoscopy combined with radial EBUS, often with fluoroscopy and VBN, improving diagnostic yield in small peripheral pulmonary lesions.
Three-dimensional guidance significantly increases diagnostic yield compared to CT-guided UTB.

clinical_procedures.notes: Standard approach; smaller forceps (1.5 mm) fit UTB channel.
Increases tissue size; improves molecular testing feasibility.
Especially useful for lesions adjacent to rEBUS images; yield increases up to 21% when combined with forceps.

diagnostic_approaches.limitations: Guided only by fluoroscopy; limited lesion localization.

diagnostic_approaches.advantages: Higher diagnostic yield for lesions <30 mm, right upper lobe, or radiographically invisible lesions.
3D positioning of lesion and tools; improved success in challenging lesions.

figures.caption: Flexible bronchoscopes. Left to right: Ultrathin 2.8 mm / 1.2 mm; Ultrathin 3.0 mm / 1.7 mm; Thin 4.0 mm / 2.0 mm; Standard 4.8 mm / 2.0 mm; Therapeutic 5.9 mm / 3.0 mm.
key_points: Defines UTB (≤3.5 mm) vs thin, standard, and therapeutic scopes
Highlights 1.7 mm channel enabling rEBUS compatibility

clinical_guidelines.recommendation: UTB should be considered as first-line for small (<30 mm) peripheral pulmonary lesions, especially when rEBUS or VBN guidance is available.
Use UTB as a second procedure when standard or thin bronchoscopy fails to achieve diagnostic rEBUS positioning.
Cryobiopsy or combined sampling (forceps + TBNA/cryobiopsy) increases yield by 15–25% compared to forceps alone.
Molecular testing success rates are lower with 1.5 mm forceps samples; consider cryobiopsy or multiple samples if NGS is required.

complications.note: Often due to visceral pleura injury from distal reach of UTB.

points: UTB reaches more distal bronchi than thin scopes (median 5th-generation vs 4th).
Randomized trials show higher diagnostic yields with UTB when combined with rEBUS/VBN.
UTB improves outcomes when added after failed thin bronchoscopy.
Integration of cryobiopsy and TBNA boosts molecular adequacy.
Complication rates remain low and comparable to conventional scopes.
